description:
This an Atlantic portfolio venture.

About the Venture

This early-stage venture is building a discovery engine for chemistry, comprising a platform for running end-to-end simulations of chemical reaction systems, and a world model + agent stack that uses the simulation platform to discover new chemistry.

Their goal is to build backend scientific data infrastructure to meet the demands of AI systems that can truly accelerate and automate the discovery layer of chemistry.

Both founders hold PhDs in Chemistry from the University of Oxford, and the venture has already secured pre-seed funding. They are now building out their founding team.

The Role

  • As a Computational Chemist, you will play a central role in shaping the scientific foundations of the venture's technology, helping develop the computational methods and workflows that underpin its end-to-end chemical reaction simulation platform.

  • You’ll work closely with researchers and engineers to integrate state-of-the-art computational chemistry methods with machine learning approaches, driving progress towards the venture's strategic and scientific objectives.

  • You’ll take ownership of developing, validating and optimising the computational chemistry components of the platform, with a particular focus on reaction mechanisms, reaction kinetics, molecular dynamics and the modelling of complex chemical environments.

  • You will design, implement and refine scalable scientific workflows for generating, processing and analysing chemical reaction data, improving the accuracy, reliability and computational efficiency of simulations.

  • Beyond your core scientific responsibilities, the team is looking for someone who can contribute to strategic research decisions, bring strong independent scientific judgement, and help shape the interdisciplinary research culture of the company at an early stage.

What You'll Work On

  • Foundation models for chemical reactivity: The team is building and training foundation models for chemical reactivity with a variety of data modalities. You'll help curate this foundational data corpus by developing cheminformatics and computational chemistry workflows for generating data from combinatorial enumeration, as well as robust data filtering, clustering and validation routines.

  • Computational methods: The team is working on efficient computational methods from which foundational data is generated and the platform is validated. You'll be responsible for developing protocols for estimating solvation and entropy factors in chemical reaction steps. This involves keeping up to date with published literature for ideas and inspiration.

  • Generative models: The venture is expanding its foundational data corpus beyond combinatorial workflows. You'll help design, validate and benchmark the generative model architectures that accomplish this.

  • Chemical reaction simulation: The team is building out an end-to-end chemical reaction simulation platform. You'll be involved in designing the architecture and assembling the platform, as well as developing benchmarks and validation protocols against computational and experimental methods.

  • World models and agents: The venture will be developing an agent + world model stack that operates on the simulation platform. You'll be responsible for formulating the action space in which the world model is trained and the agent explores new chemical reaction space.

What They're Looking For

The team is looking for someone who enjoys being given a blank canvas and the chance to create something spectacular with it. In particular, someone who brings:

  • A PhD in Computational Chemistry, Machine Learning, or a related field.

  • Intellectual curiosity: Someone who enjoys venturing outside their comfort zone, exploring new ideas and applying their knowledge and experience to unfamiliar domains.

  • An entrepreneurial mindset: Someone who thrives in an early-stage environment, enjoys building things from scratch and is excited to grow beyond the traditional boundaries of their role.

  • Independent thinking and scientific judgement: Someone who can take ownership of complex challenges, contribute new ideas and help shape the scientific direction of the venture.

  • A collaborative approach: Someone who can build strong relationships across the team and actively contribute to shaping and nurturing the company culture as it grows.

  • An instinct for building great working environments: Someone who understands the importance of the right tools, systems and ways of working to help themselves and the wider team do their best work.

title: Staff Software Engineer, Data Enrichment Platform
description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About our Data Enrichment Platform Team

Our Enrichment Orchestration team builds the platform that enables Wayve’s teams to deploy, run, evaluate and continually improve machine-learning models. Processing petabytes of driving data across large GPU fleets, the team creates dependable, self-service capabilities that help model engineers understand model performance, improve quality and reduce operational effort and cost.

As our Staff Software Engineer, you’ll own the platform’s technical vision and long-term direction. You’ll combine hands-on engineering with cross-team technical leadership, shaping how model engineering, infrastructure, compute and data capabilities come together to accelerate model development.

🧠 Your day-to-day

  • Own the technical vision and architecture for the end-to-end Data Enrichment Platform, translating user needs into a clear technical direction.

  • Lead the design, development and operation of backend services, APIs, model-execution workflows, versioned outputs, annotation capabilities and dataset catalogues.

  • Make architectural decisions for petabyte-scale data and large GPU fleets, addressing data locality, scheduling, capacity, backpressure, failure recovery, observability and cost.

  • Evaluate when to build, buy, reuse, integrate, consolidate or replace technologies as Wayve’s needs and the technology landscape evolve.

  • Establish clear technical boundaries and ownership across model engineering, AI Platform, infrastructure, compute, storage and data teams.

  • Remain hands-on while leading cross-team delivery, mentoring senior engineers and raising standards for maintainable, tested and observable software.

  • Drive adoption of reusable, self-service capabilities so teams can onboard and operate workflows independently.

  • Define measurable service levels and success metrics covering reliability, throughput, cost, automation and adoption.

🧩 What you’ll be working on

  • A scalable platform for large-scale inference, automated evaluation, model monitoring, active learning and retraining.

  • Self-service backend services and APIs that enable dozens of model engineers to deploy and operate repeatable workflows independently.

  • Reproducible dataset selection, versioned outputs, annotation workflows and dataset catalogues with clear metadata, provenance and lineage.

  • Reliable model-execution workflows operating across petabytes of driving data and large GPU fleets, scaling towards thousands of GPUs.

  • Monitoring and operational tooling that make model quality, platform reliability, throughput, cost, runtime and workflow status visible.

  • The foundations for continuous evaluation, drift detection and automated model-improvement loops across robotics and computer-vision workloads.

  • Architectural improvements that reduce inference costs, duplicate compute and manual operational effort.

🙌 You should apply if

  • You have owned the long-term technical direction of a complex, multi-system platform or capability and can demonstrate the measurable outcomes of your decisions.

  • You have strong production software-engineering experience in Python, building maintainable, tested and observable backend services, APIs and data-processing systems.

  • You have deep experience designing and operating large-scale distributed systems for data-intensive or compute-intensive workloads.

  • You have a track record of turning internal platforms into widely adopted, reliable and usable self-service products.

  • You bring excellent architecture and technology judgement, balancing immediate delivery needs with long-term platform direction.

  • You remain hands-on while leading delivery across organisational boundaries, influencing technical decisions and aligning teams around clear ownership and shared outcomes.

  • You communicate complex ideas clearly and have experience mentoring senior engineers and strengthening the technical capabilities of those around you.

  • Experience with workflow orchestration, batch inference, ML platforms, model deployment or registries would be an advantage. Relevant technologies include Flyte, Airflow, Dagster, Argo, Spark, Databricks, Ray, Kubernetes and GPU infrastructure.

  • Experience with annotation or dataset-catalogue platforms, including provenance, versioning, lineage and quality control, would also be valuable.

  • Experience with production robotics or computer-vision platforms—including annotation, inference, evaluation and model monitoring—is particularly desirable. Computer-vision research expertise is not required.

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay!

If you’re passionate about autonomy and the impact you could make at Wayve, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

More about Wayve

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end-to-end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real-world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand-coded rules or pre-mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once-in-a-generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human-driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware-agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2+ through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real-world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

How we work 💻 — Locations & Flexible Working

This role is based in London. Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

🔍 The Interview Process

Our process is clear and respectful of your time.

Initial call / Talent Partner screen (30 mins)

Competency interviews: Python coding (60 mins), System design (60 mins)

Deep Dive Interviews: Technical Leadership, Hiring Manager interview (45 mins)

Final interview: Mission, values and Staff-level calibration (45 mins)

We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.

What’s in it for you (location dependent)

💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually

📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long-term success of Wayve

✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable

✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands-on in vehicle workshops and labs

📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth

🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more

A quick, honest note before you apply.

Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.

If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.

Quantitative Researcher - 2027 Graduates
description:
At Graviton, we don't believe the best trading strategies come from following established playbooks. They come from asking better questions. Why does a pattern exist? What is driving it? Is it real or just noise? Can it be explained, modelled and turned into an edge?

As a Quantitative Researcher, you'll work on those questions every day. You'll investigate market behaviour, develop quantitative models, build and test hypotheses and turn insights into trading strategies, working alongside researchers and technologists in an environment where an idea on a whiteboard can reach live trading quickly.

This isn't a role where the answers are in a textbook. The problems are open-ended, the data is enormous, and finding the answers is the job.

Ideal candidates are rigorous thinkers who genuinely enjoy mathematics, programming and figuring out things that aren't obvious, based in our Singapore, London, Amsterdam or US offices.

What You'll Work On

You'll work across quantitative research and systematic trading, taking ideas through the full lifecycle: question, hypothesis, experiment, model, validation, strategy, production. Depending on your team and research interests, your work would include:

  • Discovering predictive patterns and sources of alpha from billions of market events
  • Formulating hypotheses about market behaviour and designing experiments to test them
  • Applying probability, statistics, optimization and machine learning to build predictive models and quantitative signals for systematic trading
  • Designing robust backtests and statistical tests to distinguish genuine signals from noise
  • Working with large and complex datasets to uncover patterns that aren't immediately visible
  • Investigating market microstructure and how markets behave at different timescales
  • Evaluating strategy performance, identifying weaknesses and continuously refining models
  • Developing research infrastructure and AI-powered tools and agents that make experimentation faster and analysis deeper
  • Working closely with technologists to translate research ideas into efficient, production-ready systems
  • Exploring new techniques in machine learning, statistics and quantitative finance to uncover new sources of edge

No two research problems are the same. Good research finds patterns. Great research understands why they exist.

What Success Looks Like

Successful researchers at Graviton discover new sources of alpha and turn them into robust trading strategies, build models that hold up under real market conditions and not only in backtests, develop a deep understanding of market behaviour, create research frameworks and tools that make the broader team more effective, work with technologists to take ideas from research into production, and communicate complex quantitative ideas clearly and rigorously. Your impact isn't measured by how many models you build. It's measured by the quality of the ideas you discover and what those ideas enable.

Who We're Looking For

We're looking for exceptional problem solvers who genuinely enjoy mathematics, programming and figuring out things that aren't obvious.

  • Degree in a quantitative discipline such as mathematics, physics, computer science, statistics, operations research or machine learning
  • No active backlogs
  • Strong programming skills in Python and/or C++
  • Solid grounding in probability, statistics, linear algebra and optimization, with experience in machine learning, statistical modelling or data analysis, whether through coursework, research or personal projects
  • Comfort working with large, complex datasets, and strong analytical thinking
  • A passion for applying quantitative thinking and rigorous research to solve open-ended problems in markets
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex ideas clearly

Prior exposure to quantitative research, algorithmic trading, market microstructure, competitive mathematics or machine learning is valuable, but we care more about how you think than whether you've worked in finance before.

Our Culture

More than specific tools or techniques, we care how you think. We look for people who are curious enough to keep asking why, analytical enough to separate signal from noise, persistent enough to pursue difficult problems, intellectually honest enough to abandon an idea when the evidence says so, and humble enough to keep learning.

At Graviton, researchers sit alongside technologists on specialized trading teams that operate with significant autonomy. You'll have meaningful ownership of research problems from day one: forming your own hypotheses, challenging existing approaches and following the evidence wherever it leads, with the infrastructure and datasets to test ideas at scale, competitive compensation, and a culture where the best idea wins regardless of who proposed it.

Markets are among the most complex systems humans have ever created, and they never stop changing. Neither should our thinking. Every day, someone asks a better question and finds an answer nobody had. That someone could be you.

title: Quality Systems Lead
description:
About us

Encord is the universal data layer for AI that helps 300+ AI teams train and run models on the right data. Our platform indexes, curates, annotates, and evaluates data across the full AI lifecycle, from development through production.

 

Trusted by Woven by Toyota, AXA, UiPath, Zipline, and more. We're an ambitious team of 100+ working at the frontier of AI and have raised $60M in Series C funding from Wellington Management, CRV, Next47 and Y Combinator.

 

The role

We're hiring a Quality Systems Lead to own how Encord measures the quality of the human data we deliver to frontier AI labs, physical AI companies and enterprise AI teams — the standard itself, the systems that evaluate against it, and the audit function that produces the ground truth behind both. Data quality is what our customers buy. As we scale across data types — image and video, document, medical, LLM evaluation, robot teleoperation, egocentric capture — quality coverage cannot scale linearly with headcount. So this role has two halves that make each other work. You will build automated evaluation: model-assisted and LLM-based screening, agreement analysis at scale, anomaly and drift detection across annotation output. And you will build and run a dedicated audit team of around ten specialists in India, whose judgements become the labelled ground truth that trains and calibrates that automated layer. As coverage automates, the audit team moves up to the cases models can't judge and to generating gold sets for each new data type we take on. It is an unusual combination — engineering and consistent QC operations in one person — and it is the combination the job needs. You will also have an advantage your counterparts elsewhere in the industry don't: Encord owns the platform this work runs on, so the measurement you build can become native capability in the product rather than internal tooling.

 

What you'll do

  • Build automated dataset quality evaluation and root-cause detection — model-assisted and LLM-as-judge screening, agreement analysis at scale, anomaly and drift detection across annotation output

  • Hire, train, calibrate and manage a dedicated audit team of around ten specialists based in our India operation, held to inter-rater agreement and catch rate rather than volume audited

  • Turn audit output into labelled ground truth that trains and validates the automated layer, and manage the ratio of automated to manual coverage deliberately over time

  • Own the quality standard for every data type we deliver — written rubrics with worked edge cases, golden sets, and acceptance criteria agreed with the customer, alongside the Special Projects lead, before the first batch ships

  • Build scoring systems that rank annotator and reviewer performance and feed routing, staffing and offboarding decisions

  • Set the pass thresholds that certification gates on, so nobody works a project queue without having demonstrated they meet the standard

  • Report quality KPIs to leadership, and into the reporting our Special Projects leads take to customers: accuracy against client spec, inter-annotator agreement, rework rate, cost of rework, and coverage

  • Work with Project Management on remediation — you produce the measurement and the diagnosis, production owns fixing the project, and the standard stays independent of the people being measured

  • Own the unit economics of quality: cost per audited unit, and the coverage you buy per pound spent

  • Partner with Product and Engineering to bring quality measurement into Encord platform as native capability

Who we're looking for

  • You build and you operate. You'll write the evaluation pipeline, and you'll also run the weekly calibration session with ten auditors in another country

  • Your instinct on a coverage problem is to automate it — you reach for a model, a heuristic or a better sampling design before you reach for more auditors

  • Statistically literate in a practical way: sampling design, agreement statistics, and the judgement to spot a metric being optimised against rather than met

  • You can hold a calibrated standard across a distributed team you don't sit with — you know that ten uncalibrated auditors produce ten standards

  • A strong writer. Much of this job is producing rubrics a distributed workforce can follow without you in the room

  • You hold a standard under commercial pressure, and you bring the evidence that makes it stick with a delivery team or a client

  • Systems thinker: as interested in why a failure recurs across projects as in this project's defect rate

 

Experience requirements

  • 4+ years owning both technical and operational outcomes in a data, AI or service delivery environment where quality was measured rather than asserted

  • Hands-on Python and SQL. You build the analysis and the tooling rather than specify it for someone else

  • Practical experience applying models to a quality or evaluation problem — LLM-as-judge, model-assisted QA, automated evaluation, anomaly detection or classifier-based screening

  • Sampling methodology and agreement statistics (Cohen's and Fleiss' kappa, F1 against ground truth) applied to real production data

  • Experience hiring, training and managing a team, ideally an audit, review or QA team, and ideally distributed

  • Track record of building a quality framework or function, including the reporting leadership and customers run on

  • Bonus: direct experience of annotation, evaluation or model-training workflows, and of what frontier AI labs accept as evidence of quality

  • Bonus: a STEM degree, or a background in data science or research engineering

  • Bonus: multilingual delivery and linguistic quality assessment

 

Why Encord

  • Competitive salary, commission, and equity in a high-growth startup

  • Strong in-person culture — most of the team works from our London office 4+ days/week

  • 25 days annual leave + UK public holidays

  • Annual learning & development budget

  • Travel for customer visits, events, and conferences across the UK and Europe

  • Company lunches twice a week

  • Monthly socials & bi-annual team offsites

The Data Science team builds the AI models behind Beamery's Data Foundry, the common data and AI layer powering all Beamery products, and works hand in hand with the product teams to empower their features with AI (such as Talent Match and recommendations). At the heart of our work is the Beamery taxonomy, the language of work (skills, role titles and tasks) that every Beamery product speaks, built on more than a decade of research and kept current by the Taxonomist, our agentic system, so it reflects the real pulse of the job market. We see ourselves as pioneers in AI for HR Tech: in 2026 the team finished 1st in the industry track and 2nd overall out of 40 teams at the ACM RecSys Challenge.

  • Strong experience with recommender systems, search, ranking or matching (e.g. learning-to-rank, scoring models, Gradient Boosting Trees, embedding models).

  • Fluency in evaluation: designing datasets and quality metrics (such as AUC, NDCG, precision and recall), and using LLM-as-a-judge and human feedback.

  • A strong foundation in NLP and GenAI, including Transformers, LLMs and embedding models (training or fine-tuning them is a strong plus).

Drawing on deep regulatory knowledge, you will lead Consumer Duty initiatives, actively spot potential customer harm, examine what drives customer journeys, and ensure targeted remediation creates lasting, positive impact.

You'll need sharp analytical skills and the confidence to influence stakeholders, translating data and MI into decisive action. You will construct and manage dashboards and reporting mechanisms that illuminate emerging patterns, vulnerable customer risks, and key concerns, offering executive leadership clear visibility into operational gaps and necessary solutions.

Your contribution goes well beyond producing MI. You will conduct QA across complex complaint handling and sensitive customer interactions, manage Ombudsman cases, and speak up when evidence shows outcomes aren't meeting expectations. Collaborating across teams, you'll turn data-driven insights into practical improvements, drive projects to completion, and evaluate whether changes deliver real results for our users.

We're seeking someone who views Consumer Duty as a powerful driver of business improvement rather than a routine compliance exercise. You'll bring together technical understanding, rigorous analysis, and constructive challenge to investigate root causes, align key partners, deliver change, and prove that customer experiences are continuously getting better.

Who you’ll be working with and reporting to

You'll work closely with teams across Customer Support, Complaints, Compliance, Risk, Operations, Product, Data, Technology, and other business functions.

The role will have broad exposure across the organisation, particularly when customer outcome risks or Consumer Duty-related remediation require cross-functional action.

You'll also work closely with senior stakeholders through Consumer Duty governance and reporting, helping translate detailed analysis into clear insights, risks, recommendations, and actions.

What you’ll be doing

As a Consumer Duty Specialist, you will:

  • Turn data into customer outcome insight: Build and own MI, dashboards, KPIs, and reporting that give the business a clear view of customer outcomes, trends, risks, and emerging areas of concern.

  • Own Consumer Duty reporting: Produce monthly and quarterly Consumer Duty reporting, turning complex data into a clear story for senior leadership and Board-level audiences. You'll go beyond showing what happened to explain why it matters and what we should do about it.

  • Identify customer harm: Use complaints, QA findings, customer feedback, vulnerable customer data, Ombudsman cases, and MI to identify potential customer harm, emerging risks, and systemic issues.

  • Challenge the business: Where the evidence suggests customers aren't receiving good outcomes, you'll be expected to ask difficult questions, challenge assumptions, and ensure the issue is properly understood and addressed.

  • Drive remediation and change: Work with stakeholders across the business to agree remediation plans, establish clear owners and timelines, and help drive Consumer Duty-related projects and improvements through to completion.

  • Provide complaints QA: Conduct weekly quality reviews of complaints handled by the Complaints Manager, using findings to identify quality issues, customer risks, and wider trends.

  • Manage Ombudsman activity: Act as the primary operational contact with the UK Ombudsman, managing referred complaints, responses, remedies, compensation, invoices, and related communications.

  • Leverage AI and smart automation: Spot opportunities to apply automated tools and AI to scale and streamline Consumer Duty analytics, monitoring, and workflows. You will feel empowered to test emerging tech and eliminate repetitive manual work, maintaining proper critical evaluation and human governance whenever compliance risks or customer impacts are involved.

What you bring

You’ll thrive in this role if you have:

  • Strong Consumer Duty knowledge: You understand the principles of Consumer Duty and how they translate into practical customer outcomes, particularly across complaints, customer support, vulnerable customers, and customer journeys.

  • Strong data and MI experience: You know how to take complex data, build meaningful dashboards and reporting, and identify the insights that actually matter. You're comfortable working with data rather than simply consuming reports created by others.

  • A customer outcome mindset: You're naturally curious about how customers are experiencing the business and are able to connect data, customer feedback, complaints, and operational activity to real customer outcomes.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills: You can spot trends, anomalies, and patterns, investigate root causes, and determine whether an issue is isolated or potentially systemic.

  • The confidence to challenge: You're comfortable questioning decisions, processes, and assumptions when the evidence suggests customers may be experiencing poor outcomes. You can challenge constructively and build relationships at the same time.

  • A bias towards action: You don't believe reporting is the end of the process. You want to understand what needs to change, bring people together, and help make it happen.

  • Project and remediation experience: You're comfortable managing actions, timelines, dependencies, stakeholders, and risks across cross-functional projects, particularly where there is a regulatory, customer, or operational outcome to deliver.

  • An AI and automation mindset: You're naturally curious about how AI and automation can make processes more efficient, improve analysis, and free up time for higher-value work. You look for sensible opportunities to automate repetitive tasks and use AI to augment your thinking, while maintaining appropriate human oversight, critical judgement, and accountability — particularly where customer outcomes or regulatory decisions are involved.

Why is this role a good fit for you

This role is a good fit for you if:

  • You love using data to uncover things that others might not see.

  • You want your analysis to drive real change, rather than sit in a report or dashboard.

  • You enjoy asking "why?" and getting to the root cause of customer problems.

  • You're comfortable challenging the business when the evidence tells you something isn't working.

This role is not a good fit for you if:

  • You prefer to produce reporting without being involved in what happens afterwards.

  • You're uncomfortable challenging stakeholders or having difficult conversations when customer outcomes aren't where they should be.

  • You prefer working within a narrow functional remit rather than across multiple teams.

How you’ll develop in this role

In your first 6 months at Pleo, you'll:

  • Build a deep understanding of our customer outcome data, existing Consumer Duty MI, complaints, vulnerable customer journeys, and current areas of risk.

  • Take ownership of key Consumer Duty dashboards and reporting, developing a clear view of the metrics and insights that matter most.

  • Establish strong relationships with stakeholders across Customer Support, Complaints, Compliance, Risk, Operations, Product, Data, and Technology.

  • Lead the analysis behind Consumer Duty reporting and help shape how customer outcomes are presented to senior stakeholders and the Board.

Over time, you'll have the opportunity to shape how Pleo measures, understands, and improves customer outcomes, helping move Consumer Duty from a regulatory obligation into a genuine driver of better customer experiences and better business decisions.

Show me the benefits!

  • Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!)

  • Lunch is on us for your work days - enjoy catered meals or receive a lunch allowance based on your local office

  • Comprehensive private healthcare - depending on your location, coverage options include Vitality, Alan or Médis

  • We offer 25 days of holiday + your public holidays

  • For our Team, we offer both hybrid and fully remote working options

  • Option to purchase 5 additional days of holiday through a salary sacrifice

  • We use MyndUp to give our employees access to free mental health and well-being support with great success so far

  • Paid parental leave - we want to make sure that we're supportive of families and help you feel that you don't have to compromise your family due to work


The interview process

We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows:

  1. Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background.

  2. Meet the Hiring Manager: 1hr going through role in more depth.

  3. Pleo Challenge: A case study were you talk us through how you'd solve a work appropriate challenge.

Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success!

Last time we advertised this role, we received a really high volume of applications but could only select so many. Some of the key reasons why previous candidates didn’t make it past the application screening stage include:

  • CV writing and content: we receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI—it’s a big focus for us internally too—but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light. What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on. A final note: including links to your previous companies' websites is a huge help and allows us to truly understand your background!

  • Application care: every single application we receive is reviewed by a human (yes, hundreds of them) because we believe that candidates' efforts should be matched by an equal level of human care. This means that we expect a similar level of attention put into your application. Read and answer the application questions carefully, they make a huge difference in our decision-making process.

  • Profile to role fit: highlight most important aspects of the role, points that might get misunderstood, any specific industry requirements etc.

About your application

  • English first. Since it's our company language, please submit your application in English. You’ll be using it a lot if you join us.

  • A fair look for everyone. Our talent team reads every single application to ensure the process is fair. To keep things running smoothly, we only accept applications through our system—our support team can’t pass on calls or emails.

  • Diversity drives us. We can only reach our goals if our team reflects the world around us. That starts with you hitting apply, even if you don't tick every single box. We encourage people from all backgrounds and experiences to join us.

  • Interview at your best. We want you to feel comfortable throughout the process. If you have any accessibility requirements or need a specific format, email ----- We’ll design a process that works for you.

  • Your data is safe. When you apply, we process your personal data as a data processor. For more information on how Pleo processes personal data, read our Privacy Policy here.

  • Applying for multiple roles? Nothing is stopping you, and we assess every role independently. However, we do look for alignment, so make sure you can explain why your interest and experience are right for each specific role.

  • Reapplying. If you’re applying for the same role again, please wait six months from your last decision before hitting submit.

What You Bring


You care deeply about customer outcomes and you know that transformation has to be designed and led. You're proactive, strategic and comfortable steering demanding, senior stakeholders through significant change. You take pride in being the reason customers adopt, grow and succeed.

We're looking for:

● Experience building tailored transformation roadmaps and adoption plans and steering them to measurable outcomes.
● A track record of driving adoption, retention and satisfaction with enterprise clients and senior stakeholders.

● Strong programme and project management skills; you keep multi-workstream initiatives moving and your clients confident.

● Willingness to travel internationally around 25% of the time.

title: Performance Engineer
description:
UK | Full-Time

The Mission: Source.dev

Our founders spent over a decade at Google shaping the Android operating systems - building and shipping the software that now runs on billions of devices. They didn't just use Android; they led teams responsible for the Android Virtualization Framework, Security, and the Android Runtime (ART).

Through that journey, they saw a quiet but massive crisis: as device software grew in complexity, the tools used to build it remained stuck in the past. Today, a standard Android checkout exceeds 200GB of code, and builds can take hours. This "wait time" is the single biggest tax on innovation.

Source.dev was founded to reimagine software development workflows for device makers. We’re building a new generation of software tools that make building complex device software feel as simple as building a webpage - starting with SourceFS.

The Core Product: SourceFS

SourceFS is a high-performance virtual filesystem designed to turn multi-hour workflows into minutes.

  • 10x Faster Builds: Intelligent caching and virtualization that only materializes files when they are actually needed.

  • 10x Lower Costs: Enabling a standard 16-vCPU machine to outperform even a 128-vCPU machine.

  • True Engineering Productivity: Replaying hundreds of thousands of build steps instantly when inputs match.

The Cultural Anchor: Own It

We operate with a high degree of trust and a shared value of End-to-End Ownership:

"We own our work end-to-end, from spark to finish. It’s about more than just tasks; it’s the dedication to see things through, staying curious to solve problems, thinking from first principles and ensuring we fix our customer’s problems in the best possible way.”

The Role: Pushing the Speed Limits of Rust, Linux & I/O

We are looking for a Performance / Systems Engineer to join us at Source.dev. In this role, your primary metric of success is speed. You will dissect execution paths, eliminate kernel-space context-switching costs, optimize memory layouts, and ensure SourceFS runs as close to the hardware limits as physically possible.

What You’ll Work On

  • System Bottleneck Hunting: Profile, trace, and eliminate latency across CPU, memory, and disk I/O bottlenecks in Rust systems code using tools like perf, eBPF, valgrind, and custom microbenchmarks.

  • Kernel & File System Tuning: Deep dive into Linux kernel interactions, optimizing FUSE drivers, VFS caches, asynchronous I/O (io_uring), memory-mapped execution, and thread scheduling.

  • Memory & Cache Efficiency: Optimize data structures for cache locality, minimize allocation overhead, and eliminate unnecessary memory copies across boundary transitions.

  • Benchmarking Infrastructure: Design robust, reproducible benchmarking suites to measure micro- and macro-performance regression in high-concurrency environments.

  • Scaling Build Primitives: Squeeze peak performance out of massive build graphs (Android, Yocto, and more) running on high-core hardware configurations.

Ideal Candidate Profile:

  • The Performance Systems Mindset: You have a deep understanding of computer architecture (CPU caches, memory barriers, SIMD, system calls) and proven experience writing hyper-optimized code in Rust or C/C++.(or other). No prior experience with Rust required, just a willingness to learn is all we are looking for.

  • Scale-Obsessed: You have experience with (or a burning desire to fix) large-scale build systems and developer tooling.

  • Impact-Driven: You embody the "Own It" mentality - you see a friction point in the developer journey and you don’t stop until it’s gone.

  • Curious & Collaborative: You enjoy translating real-world customer problems into robust, production-grade solutions.

  • Low Ego, High Impact: Beyond being a brilliant coder, you are a thoughtful and empathetic teammate - someone who leads with kindness

  • Feedback Culture Champion: You embrace feedback and provide it thoughtfully; you see open, honest communication as the foundation of great teamwork.

 

A Note on Our Search

We are looking for the best talent, wherever it may be. If you’re on the fence about whether you’re a perfect fit, please do apply - we value diverse backgrounds and unique problem-solving approaches.

Why Join Source.dev?

  • AI-Native Infrastructure: We merge deep systems expertise with AI to solve the "impossible" - using AI to automate complex merges and conflict resolution for the next generation of devices.

  • Architect the Future: Have a direct, visible impact on the infrastructure used to build the world’s most advanced hardware.

  • Early-Stage Ownership: You’ll have a seat at the table to shape our technical roadmap, product direction, and culture from day one.

  • Tier-One Partnerships: Work side-by-side with world-class customers, from global automotive giants to leading cloud providers.

  • Elite Engineering Culture: Join a high-trust & passionate team of engineers

title: People & Workplace Experience Manager
description:
About Dust

Work is being rewritten, and the people holding the pen are the ones who actually run it.

With enterprise-grade governance, flexible model choice, and a collaborative interface for humans and agents to work together, Dust empowers AI Operators at the world’s fastest-moving companies to rewire how work gets done.

With 70%+ weekly active users, people stick with Dust as much as they do with Slack and Notion. We don't get piloted and shelved. We land once, and spread. We're at an exciting stage of our journey, and growing fast.

We're serving great customers like Datadog, 1Password, Cursor, Clay, Vanta and Persona, and aim to x5 our growth by the end of 2026.

Dust is backed by Sequoia with a determined team of optimists (coming from Stripe, OpenAI, and Stanford) who like to focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously while doing so. The Generalist named us among the Future 50.

The role

Dust is growing fast, and we want every person who joins us to feel welcome, supported, connected and able to do their best work. As our People Experience Manager, you'll shape how people experience Dust, from their first day and the moments that bring us together to the way our offices in Paris, London, New York and San Francisco support the team.

We're looking for someone who is operationally excellent and creatively ambitious. You'll handle the details carefully, and you'll also look for ways to make the employee experience much better. One day you might be redesigning part of onboarding, the next planning a company offsite, acting on survey feedback, or working with a site lead to improve one of our offices.

This role works as a partner across the company. You'll work most closely with People Operations, who lead on the core people processes. Together, you'll make sure the employee experience is well run behind the scenes and thoughtful in how people actually experience it. In Paris, you'll also work closely with our Office Manager, who runs our HQ on site and leads much of our day-to-day office life and events. In London, New York and San Francisco, you'll coordinate with local site leads. You'll also work with IT, Finance, Legal, Marketing, leadership and outside partners. Your guiding principle: consistency where it matters, local adaptation where it creates a better experience.

What you will do:

Own the employee journey

  • Own the onboarding experience end to end, working closely with our People Ops Specialist, from pre-boarding and equipment to first-day logistics and the first few weeks, so new joiners can contribute from day one in every location.

  • Work with People Ops, IT, Finance, hiring managers, our Paris Office Manager and site leads so every handoff in the employee journey is smooth.

  • Partner with People Ops and IT on offboarding, so people leave with the same care they got when they joined.

  • Be a trusted point of contact for everyday employee questions and needs, and know when to bring in People Ops.

Build culture and community

  • Run and improve our team rituals, including weekly lunches, team drinks, dinners and company gatherings.

  • Organise one or two company offsites or retreats each year.

  • Create moments that help people connect, celebrate progress and feel they belong, across offices and time zones.

  • Pay attention to the details that make experiences feel personal and inclusive, such as dietary needs, accessibility, preferences and team milestones.

  • Partner with People and Marketing on selected external and brand-building events.

Listen and turn feedback into action

  • Build feedback loops (surveys, conversations, informal check-ins) to understand how people experience Dust.

  • Turn what people tell us into concrete recommendations and visible improvements.

  • Define and track simple, useful measures of employee and workplace experience.

  • Communicate clearly and consistently about updates, events, practical information and team norms. Be assertive when needed.

Shape our workplaces

  • Make sure our offices are safe, welcoming, functional and ergonomic, and that they reflect how we want people to feel at Dust.

  • Work with our office manager on day-to-day operations: supplies, maintenance, access, equipment and services.

  • Manage workplace vendors, contracts and budget, and look for efficient ways to improve the experience.

  • Spot operational needs early and fix issues before they disrupt anyone.

Scale the experience as Dust grows

  • Help shape how our physical, hybrid and digital environments evolve as the company grows.

  • Set up simple, scalable processes and clear ownership across People, IT, Finance and Legal topics.

  • Keep the employee experience personal and high quality without making it bureaucratic.


What success looks like

After your first 100 days, you will have:

  • Built a smooth, consistent onboarding experience for every new joiner, in every location.

  • Delivered team rituals, events and offsites that strengthen connection and culture.

  • Set up feedback loops and a practical set of metrics that guide People Experience decisions.

  • Created well-run, welcoming offices where operational issues are handled quickly and proactively.

  • Established clear processes and ownership across People, workplace, IT, Finance and Legal.

  • Helped Dust grow its employee experience without it becoming bureaucratic or impersonal.

What we are looking for

  • 4+ years of experience in People Operations, People Experience, Workplace Experience in a fast growing, globally distributed environment

  • A proactive generalist who can handle many kinds of work at once without losing sight of the bigger picture.

  • Real ideas, sound judgement and the confidence to improve how things work today.

  • Strong operational ownership, project management skills and attention to detail.

  • Warmth, empathy and a genuine interest in helping people feel comfortable and connected.

  • Clear, direct, thoughtful communication, and discretion with sensitive situations.

  • Confidence working with vendors, budgets and outside partners.

  • The ability to build simple processes that scale, and to keep a high bar for quality while staying pragmatic.

  • Comfort with a fast-moving environment where priorities can change, working on your own while collaborating across the company.

Location

We're prioritizing building our team with an in-person culture at our offices in Paris, London, San Francisco, and New York because we value the magic that happens when talented people work closely together.

We have an office-first culture. Some of the best things about building at Dust are the energy, the fast decisions, and the unexpected conversations that unlock a hard problem, which happen because we are in the same room. Being together is not a formality, it is how we do our best work, and it is something we actively protect.

That said, we hire people with strong judgement and we extend that trust to how they manage their time. When working from home makes more sense for what you need to get done that day, we trust you to make that call.

Why Dust

The models are powerful enough. What's missing is the product layer where AI meets how companies actually work. That's what we're building: the infrastructure that lets any team turn scattered knowledge and tools into coordinated execution with agents they build, own, and run themselves.

We use Dust ourselves every day. We get to shape how humans and agents collaborate while solving our own problems with the product we ship. That loop is rare, and it's why we move fast.

If you're excited about defining a new category and want to join a determined team of optimists who focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously, we'd love to talk.

Even if you don't check every box in our requirements, we encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and backgrounds, and we're more interested in your potential and passion than a perfect match to our checklist.

Learn how we think and work.

  • Our product constitution, a story about our mission

  • Your Next Co-Worker Isn’t Human, Stanislas Polu, VivaTech 2026. A conversation about AI agents taking on larger parts of work and how teams collaborate with them.

  • Dust: Gabriel Hubert on Enterprise AI, Gabriel Hubert, Nasdaq, published May 7, 2026. On Dust’s approach to enterprise AI and building the company in Europe.

title: Directeur de Projet DATA CENTER
description:
Direction de Projets – Ingénierie, Construction & Infrastructures Critiques

1. Présentation du poste

Intitulé : Directeur de Projet Data Center (Data Center Project Director)

Rattachement hiérarchique : Directeur des Opérations / Directeur de Programme / Direction Générale

Périmètre : France et International

Secteur : Data Centers – Infrastructures critiques – Construction – Ingénierie

2. Mission principale

Le Directeur de Projet Data Center assure le pilotage stratégique, technique, opérationnel et financier de projets complexes de conception, de construction, d'extension ou de transformation de Data Centers.

Il garantit la bonne exécution des projets dans le respect des engagements contractuels, des budgets, des délais, des exigences de qualité, de sécurité, de performance énergétique et de disponibilité des infrastructures.

Il intervient sur l'ensemble du cycle de vie des projets, depuis les études de faisabilité jusqu'à la réception des installations, leur mise en service et leur transfert aux équipes d'exploitation.

Véritable chef d'orchestre, il coordonne les différentes parties prenantes et assure l'interface entre la maîtrise d'ouvrage, la maîtrise d'œuvre, les bureaux d'études, les entreprises de construction, les fournisseurs et les exploitants.

3. Responsabilités principales

A. Direction et pilotage stratégique des projets

  • Définir la stratégie globale d'exécution et les objectifs du projet.

  • Piloter des projets de Data Centers neufs (Greenfield), d'extension ou de rénovation (Brownfield).

  • Superviser toutes les phases du projet, de la faisabilité à la livraison.

  • Définir les jalons, les livrables et les indicateurs de performance.

  • Mettre en place la gouvernance et les instances de décision.

  • Arbitrer les choix techniques, économiques et organisationnels.

  • Anticiper les risques et définir les plans d'atténuation.

  • Assurer le reporting auprès de la Direction Générale, des investisseurs et des clients.

B. Management technique et coordination des études

Superviser et coordonner l'ensemble des disciplines techniques :

Électricité – Courants forts et faibles

  • Réseaux HTB/HTA/BT et postes de transformation.

  • Tableaux électriques, TGBT et distribution électrique.

  • Groupes électrogènes et systèmes d'alimentation secourue.

  • Onduleurs (UPS), batteries et systèmes de distribution.

  • Architectures de redondance N+1, 2N et autres configurations adaptées aux exigences de disponibilité.

  • Coordination des protections électriques, sélectivité et continuité de service.

CVC – Refroidissement et traitement d'air

  • Production et distribution frigorifique.

  • Groupes froids, free cooling et refroidissement adiabatique.

  • CRAH, CRAC et Fan Walls.

  • Systèmes de refroidissement liquide (Liquid Cooling).

  • CDU et solutions de Direct-to-Chip Cooling.

  • Optimisation des performances thermiques et énergétiques.

Bâtiment et infrastructures

  • Génie civil, structure et architecture.

  • VRD et raccordements aux réseaux.

  • Sécurité incendie et systèmes de détection/extinction.

  • Contrôle d'accès, vidéosurveillance et sûreté physique.

  • BMS, DCIM, GTB et supervision technique.

  • Intégration des infrastructures IT et télécoms.

Assurer la cohérence technique des études, la gestion des interfaces et la conformité aux exigences contractuelles et réglementaires.

C. Pilotage des études et de la conception

  • Superviser les études de faisabilité et les avant-projets.

  • Piloter les phases de conception selon les référentiels contractuels applicables, notamment RIBA 0 à 4 pour les projets concernés.

  • Valider les choix architecturaux et techniques.

  • Organiser les revues de conception et les analyses de risques.

  • Superviser la coordination BIM et les études de synthèse.

  • Garantir la constructibilité, la maintenabilité et l'exploitabilité des installations.

  • Piloter les démarches de Value Engineering.

  • Optimiser le CAPEX sans compromettre les exigences de performance et de résilience.

D. Direction de la construction et de l'exécution

  • Définir la stratégie de réalisation et le phasage des travaux.

  • Superviser les entreprises générales, les lots techniques et les sous-traitants.

  • Coordonner les équipes de maîtrise d'œuvre et de construction.

  • Garantir le respect des plannings et des jalons contractuels.

  • Piloter les interfaces entre génie civil, électricité, CVC et infrastructures IT.

  • Superviser les procédures de contrôle qualité.

  • Veiller au respect des exigences HSE.

  • Gérer les modifications, non-conformités et situations critiques.

  • Organiser les opérations préalables à la réception.

E. Gestion financière et contractuelle

  • Construire et piloter le budget global du projet.

  • Superviser les engagements financiers et le suivi des dépenses.

  • Piloter les CAPEX et les prévisions à terminaison (Estimate at Completion).

  • Identifier les dérives budgétaires et mettre en œuvre les actions correctives.

  • Superviser les consultations, appels d'offres et négociations.

  • Piloter les contrats de maîtrise d'œuvre, d'ingénierie, de construction et de fourniture.

  • Gérer les avenants, réclamations contractuelles et risques financiers.

  • Optimiser les coûts et préserver les marges du projet.

  • Assurer un reporting financier fiable et régulier.

F. Commissioning et mise en service

  • Définir et superviser la stratégie de commissioning.

  • Coordonner les essais des équipements et systèmes techniques.

  • Superviser les essais fonctionnels et les essais intégrés (Integrated Systems Testing).

  • Vérifier les scénarios de fonctionnement normal, dégradé et secouru.

  • Piloter la levée des réserves et la clôture des non-conformités.

  • Garantir la remise des DOE, procédures et documentations techniques.

  • Organiser la formation des équipes d'exploitation.

  • Superviser le transfert opérationnel vers les équipes Facilities Management et Data Center Operations.

G. Management des équipes et des parties prenantes

  • Encadrer les chefs de projet, Design Managers, Construction Managers et responsables techniques.

  • Coordonner les bureaux d'études, consultants et partenaires.

  • Définir les responsabilités et les objectifs des équipes.

  • Animer les réunions de pilotage et les comités de direction.

  • Développer une culture de performance, de sécurité et de collaboration.

  • Gérer les situations conflictuelles et les arbitrages complexes.

  • Assurer une communication structurée avec les clients et investisseurs.

4. Compétences techniques requises

Ingénierie Data Center

  • Excellente compréhension des architectures électriques et mécaniques des Data Centers.

  • Maîtrise des enjeux de disponibilité, de résilience et de redondance.

  • Connaissance des référentiels EN 50600, ISO/IEC 22237, des exigences Uptime Institute et des recommandations ASHRAE applicables.

  • Compréhension des contraintes liées aux infrastructures IT à haute densité.

  • Connaissance des enjeux de performance énergétique, notamment PUE et WUE.

Gestion de projets complexes

  • Maîtrise des méthodes de planification et de gestion des risques.

  • Pilotage de projets multidisciplinaires à forts enjeux financiers.

  • Gestion contractuelle et financière.

  • Maîtrise des processus de conception, construction et commissioning.

  • Expérience des environnements EPC, EPCM, Design & Build ou maîtrise d'ouvrage.

Outils

  • Microsoft Project / Primavera P6.

  • AutoCAD / Revit / Navisworks.

  • Environnements BIM.

  • Power BI et outils de reporting.

  • Outils de suivi budgétaire et de gestion documentaire.

5. Profil recherché

Formation

  • Diplôme d'ingénieur ou formation supérieure Bac+5 en génie électrique, énergétique, mécanique, bâtiment ou construction.

  • Une spécialisation en infrastructures critiques ou Data Centers constitue un atout.

Expérience

  • Expérience professionnelle significative, idéalement 12 à 15 ans minimum, en gestion de projets techniques complexes.

  • Expérience confirmée en direction de projets de construction ou d'ingénierie de Data Centers.

  • Expérience dans la gestion de projets à budgets importants et équipes multidisciplinaires.

  • Bonne connaissance des processus de conception, construction et mise en service.

  • Expérience internationale appréciée.

Langues

  • Français courant.

  • Anglais professionnel indispensable, à l'écrit comme à l'oral.

6. Compétences managériales et comportementales

  • Leadership et capacité à fédérer des équipes pluridisciplinaires.

  • Vision stratégique et forte orientation résultats.

  • Excellentes capacités d'analyse et de décision.

  • Maîtrise des enjeux financiers et contractuels.

  • Capacité à anticiper et à gérer les situations critiques.

  • Rigueur, organisation et sens des responsabilités.

  • Excellentes aptitudes relationnelles et de négociation.

  • Capacité à communiquer avec des interlocuteurs techniques et exécutifs.

  • Orientation client et culture de l'engagement.

7. Rémunération

La rémunération proposée pour ce poste s'établit entre EUR 12,000 et 20,000 par mois.

description:
Résumé

Nous recherchons un(e) Associate Team Lead Support N2 / Chef(fe) d’équipe Support N2 pour rejoindre l’équipe Support Niveau 2 de Pennylane, au service des dirigeants d’entreprise et des cabinets comptables.

Pennylane est une plateforme de gestion financière et comptable qui accompagne les dirigeants d’entreprise et les cabinets d’expertise comptable dans leur quotidien. L’équipe Support Niveau 2 intervient sur les demandes les plus complexes ou nécessitant une expertise métier et produit approfondie, en lien avec les équipes Support Niveau 1, Support Technique, Produit et Tech.

Ce rôle est un poste de management de proximité : tu seras le relais opérationnel du Team Lead Support N2 et accompagneras une équipe de 6 à 12 agents au quotidien pour leur permettre de répondre aux utilisateurs avec efficacité, qualité et empathie. Tu contribueras également au pilotage de l’activité, à l’amélioration continue du support et à des projets transverses.

Notre culture

Au sein du Support, nous valorisons la transparence, la bonne ambiance, l’entraide et la résilience.

Nous restons proches de la réalité de nos utilisateurs, notamment des dirigeants d’entreprise et des professionnels de la comptabilité, afin de traiter chaque demande avec expertise métier, maîtrise du produit et empathie. Cette approche s’inscrit dans la culture Pennylane de Supporting SMEs et de proximité avec les utilisateurs.

Nous encourageons le feedback dans les deux sens, le développement de chacun et la prise d’initiative. Nous accordons de l’importance à l’autonomie, à la responsabilité et à la confiance, dans l’esprit de Community of Builders et de Radical Trust.

Concrètement, ton quotidien ressemblera à ça

  • Animer les points d’équipe et suivre la charge quotidienne.

  • Accompagner les agents sur leurs tickets, leurs priorités et leurs situations complexes.

  • Réaliser des écoutes ou analyses de conversations pour donner du feedback constructif.

  • Suivre les indicateurs de performance et de qualité de l’équipe, comme le temps de première réponse, le temps de résolution, la satisfaction client et le volume de tickets traités.

  • Participer aux rituels de pilotage opérationnel : suivi de la charge, priorisation des demandes, identification des alertes et coordination avec les autres équipes Support.

  • Remonter les irritants utilisateurs aux équipes Produit, Tech ou Ops.

  • Contribuer à améliorer les process, la documentation et les outils internes.

Responsabilités

  • Manager une équipe de 6 à 12 agents sous la supervision du Team Lead Support N2, en les accompagnant dans leur activité quotidienne, leur progression et leur épanouissement professionnel.

  • Donner des feedbacks clairs, réguliers et transparents, réaliser des écoutes et analyses de conversations, suivre les bilans et plans d’accompagnement individuels, proposer des coachings et identifier les besoins de formation.

  • Suivre les indicateurs de l’équipe et contribuer à la qualité du support, notamment le temps de première réponse, la satisfaction client, le temps de résolution, le volume traité, la prise en charge des nouveaux tickets et le suivi des tickets en cours.

  • Être force de proposition pour optimiser les process, les outils, la documentation et les modes de fonctionnement du Support.

description:
Vous cherchez un environnement professionnel stimulant basé sur l'autonomie et la confiance ?

Pennylane vous offre l'opportunité de grandir au sein d'une entreprise en pleine croissance.

Ici, votre expertise contribuera directement à aider les entrepreneurs à reprendre le contrôle de leurs finances. Découvrez un lieu où vos compétences seront valorisées et où vous pourrez façonner l'avenir de la gestion financière.

Notre vision

Notre ambition est de devenir le logiciel de pilotage financier préféré des PMEs européennes.

Nous aidons les entrepreneurs à se débarrasser des tâches chronophages liées à la comptabilité et à la finance, tout en leur donnant accès à des informations financières clés pour les aider à prendre les meilleures décisions pour leur entreprise.

Parallèlement, nous aidons les cabinets d'expertise-comptable, en leur permettant de passer moins de temps sur des tâches redondantes et répétitives, et plus de temps sur la partie conseil et accompagnement de leurs clients.

À propos de Pennylane

Pennylane est une des FinTech à la plus forte croissance en France, et souhaite bientôt adresser le marché européen.

En 5 ans d'existence, nous sommes parvenus à :

💻 Nous positionner sur le marché comme un éditeur de solution de comptabilité et de gestion financière innovant

💰 Lever un total de 400 millions d'euros, auprès d'investisseurs de renom, dont Sequoïa, le fonds phare de la Silicon Valley, connu pour avoir soutenu Google, Facebook, Airbnb, Stripe, Paypal et bien d'autres à leur début

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Passer de 7 cofondateurs à une équipe de 1000 collaborateurs, avec une note moyenne de 4,9/5 sur Glassdoor et 94% des évaluateurs Glassdoor qui recommanderaient PL à leurs proches!

🌍 Construire une équipe internationale composée de collaborateurs issus de 25 pays différents, avec une culture du télétravail très flexible

🤝 Gagner la confiance de milliers d'utilisateurs et obtenir d'excellents retours

🚀 Déjà plus de 900,000 TPE/PME et plus de 6000 cabinets d’expertise-comptable utilisent Pennylane en France !

Pourquoi ce rôle est-il si important chez nous ?

En tant que Spécialiste Support Pilotage et Comptabilité, tu te positionnes comme un expert métier et plateforme. Tu es l'interlocuteur privilégié de notre base client qui a choisi Pennylane comme logiciel central de leur gestion comptable et financière.

Tu te trouves donc au cœur de l'expérience client 360 et fais profiter les clients et leurs comptables de la pleine puissance de Pennylane au service de leur croissance.

Comment vas-tu contribuer au projet ?

En tant que membre de l'équipe Support applicatif et technique comptable, tu es le point de relais central entre nos clients Dirigeants, leurs Comptables internalisés et les Cabinets Comptable. Tu es en contact quotidien avec les utilisateurs et tu cherches à comprendre les problèmes qu'ils rencontrent.

Après investigation, ton but est d'apporter une réponse ou solution à ton interlocuteur, ou quand cela est nécessaire, d'escalader le problème aux équipes techniques. Tu as aussi la charge d'aider les comptables d’entreprises et de cabinets à intégrer leurs données sur Pennylane afin de faciliter leur migration.

Quelles seront tes missions au quotidien ?

3 premiers mois :

- Tu te formes sur le produit et les rouages de l'équipe.

- Tu apprends tout ce qu'il faut savoir sur notre entreprise, notre vision, et nos différents départements.

- Tu apprends à identifier toutes les parties prenantes et à collaborer efficacement au sein de ton équipe, ainsi qu'avec les différents départements.

- Tu commences à répondre à des demandes liées à la comptabilité : tu réceptionnes les demandes, les qualifies en t’appuyant sur une compréhension approfondie des principes comptables et apportes des réponses rapides et impactantes.

4 à 6 mois :

- Tu gagnes en autonomie et prends intégralement les commandes en assurant un bon suivi des demandes jusqu’à la résolution complète des tickets pour garantir la satisfaction des utilisateurs.

- Tu commences à gérer des demandes clients de plus en plus complexe.

- Tu contribues à la création et à l’actualisation des supports d’aide à disposition du client afin de développer leur autonomie.

- Tu partages à tes collègues tes connaissances comptables et ton expérience "terrain".

- Tu portes la voix comme l’usage du client et tu partages aux équipes produit des retours construits.

Et ensuite... :

- Tu deviens un expert produit et fais gagner en efficacité ton équipe en identifiant les axes d'amélioration.

- Tu prends le contrôle et mène au succès des projets qui te tiennent à cœur et qui te font progresser.

Dans le futur, tu auras des possibilités d'évoluer vers la résolution de questions plus pointues dans l'équipe Support mais aussi vers d'autres équipes telles que les gestionnaires de comptes ou les responsables de la mise en œuvre pour nos clients.

Compétences requises

- De formation comptable (BTS CGO, DCG, BTS assistant de gestion PME-PMI, Master CCA ou Bachelor Responsable admin et comptable).

- Expérience d'au moins 3 ans en cabinet comptable (idéalement avoir fait au moins trois périodes fiscales).

- Un travail en direct avec le dirigeant est un plus (conseil interne par exemple).

- Appétence pour les outils de travail innovants et les nouvelles technologies.

- Autonomie, capacité à résoudre des problèmes seul(e) et à trouver des solutions.

- Une connaissance de l'outil Pennylane est un plus.

- Avoir un niveau professionnel en anglais.

- Aisance rédactionnelle et pédagogue pour interagir avec les utilisateurs de manière claire et professionnelle.

- Capacité à comprendre et à répondre aux besoins des clients, à offrir un excellent service et à maintenir de bonnes relations avec les clients.

- Aptitude à travailler de manière autonome et en équipe.

- Flexibilité pour s’adapter aux évolutions rapides de l’outil.

- Volonté d’apprendre et de rester à jour sur les évolutions du produit.

🤝 Process de recrutement

● Une première rencontre avec notre Talent Acquisition Manager (30 min)

● Un second entretien et un case study en direct avec un(e) Associate Team Lead (1h)

● Un entretien final avec un(e) Team Lead (45 min)

🏥 Une mutuelle parmi les meilleures sur le marché (Alan Blue et Alan Mind)

🍜 Des tickets restaurants (Carte Swile)

🇬🇧 La possibilité de perfectionner ton anglais grâce à Busuu

🏢 Une facilité d’accès à nos bureaux, situés à quelques minutes de Saint Lazare en plein cœur de Paris

💵 Une enveloppe de BSPCE

🏃‍♀️ Un accès à 8000 salles de sport partout en France et plus de 300 activités de bien-être via notre partenaire Gymlib

💻 Un Mac

🎉 Nous pratiquons de nombreux sports ensemble et avons à cœur de nous réunir régulièrement autour d’événements d’entreprise tels que les Tech Days (qui permettent aux Pennylaners en remote de se réunir tous les 3 mois) ou notre séminaire d’entreprise qui a lieu une fois par an, et qui favorise de grands moments de cohésion pour toutes et tous.

Pour t'épanouir chez Pennylane, il faudra:

-Parler anglais (le niveau est évalué et apprécié en fonction du département auquel tu postules)

-Apprécier travailler dans un environnement en changement constant

-Faire de la collaboration une priorité au sein de son équipe ou avec d'autres parties prenantes

-Avoir un recul suffisant pour prioriser les actions à fort impact business dans son activité quotidienne.

Nous savons que certaines personnes sont moins susceptibles de postuler que d'autres si elles estiment ne pas remplir l'intégralité des critères.

Si tu hésites, nous t'encourageons à postuler quand même : qui sait, cela pourrait être le début d'une collaboration significative et durable !

Nous ne vous demanderons jamais de paiement, ni d’informations financières (coordonnées bancaires, paiement pour un entretien, achat de matériel, etc.) dans le cadre du recrutement.

Si une telle demande vous est faite, il s’agit d’une fraude. Nous vous invitons à ne pas répondre et à nous le signaler immédiatement."
